# Build task

> Builds a task of a Gradatim project's open sprint from its design, test first, and shows each acceptance criterion with its evidence. Use when the user asks for Gradatim's build task step, to build, implement or code a designed task, or to go on with a build that stopped.

| | |
|---|---|
| Skill | `build-task`, [its file](../../skills/build-task/SKILL.md) |
| Step | 8 of 14: build task |
| Runs | After the task's design |
| Next | close task |
| Call it | `/gradatim:build-task` on Claude Code; [the other hosts](install.md#calling-a-skill) |

## When to use it

- The user asks for Gradatim's build task step, or to build, implement or code a task of the open sprint, or the next one.
- The user asks to go on with a build that stopped.
- Not for a task with no design: that is [`design-task`](design-task.md). Not for a task's close, its code review or the documents it made stale: that is [`close-task`](close-task.md). Not for a new task, an urgent bug or work split off a task: that is [`new-sprint`](new-sprint.md)'s "add a task". Not for a change of the project's direction: that is [`decide-direction`](decide-direction.md), or [`write-architecture`](write-architecture.md) for the stack and the modules. Not for a folder with no Gradatim project: that is [`init-project`](init-project.md).

## What it reads and writes

| Document | Path | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Agent file | `AGENTS.md` | reads |
| Agent docs | `docs/agents/<topic>.md` | reads |
| Architecture | `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` | reads |
| Sprint rules and index | `docs/sprints/README.md` | reads |
| Sprint README | `docs/sprints/sprint-<n>/README.md` | reads, changes |
| Task file | `docs/sprints/sprint-<n>/<ID>-<slug>.md` | reads, changes |
| Design | `docs/plans/<ID>-<slug>-design.md` | reads, changes |
| Issue | `docs/issues/YYYY-MM-DD-<ID>-<topic>.md` | reads, creates, changes |

It also reads the project's code, and any document the task or its design points to, such as a decision. It writes the project's own files that the task needs, outside the map, as documents.md's rule 4 says: its code, its tests, its configuration and its CI. It changes no agent doc, runbook or architecture, since those are close task's, but through the sync for a change it took; and it changes the design only by a departure, marked under its step. It never writes a `CLAUDE.md`.
